title: Deterministic quasipolynomial-time mean-payoff games

issues.description: The finite-box comparison, uniqueness and basic-iteration facts are imported from the companion paper rather than proved here. This is a dependency, not a gap: I re-derived them independently. Take the set S where x-y reaches its maximum δ>0. On S both box inequalities are active, every vertex in S has a tight successor in S, and following successors gives a zero-sum cycle under ŵ, which (cycle-signs) rules out. The fixed point is then reached by monotone iteration from A.
issues.evidence: Main text: 'These finite-box facts ... are the only results imported from the companion'. The argument goes through for arbitrary A≤u, including negative and collapsed coordinates.

coverage:
Read Sections 1–7 in full; skimmed the outline of Sections 8–9 (energy and tropical applications) without auditing them. Checked these steps line by line:
- Prop 2.2: the band partition, both positional strategies, and the cycle-deletion prefix bounds.
- The main-call reduction (P=D0/32 ≥ nW, so the box solution h is a witness of both types).
- Lemma 3.1: peak lower bound, outside-support gap 23D/32 > D/2, support and claim thresholds, and the sub/supersolution inequalities after translation.
- Lemma 4.1: box nesting c±M±r/2 inside [A+D/8, A+7D/8], and the pivot grid of spacing p with 1024 moves per coordinate.
- Lemma 4.2: the rank R=d+B, the multipliers 4/3 ≥ ρ and (4/5)(8/5)=ρ, and that only the provisional child preserves B.
- Lemmas 5.1/5.2: exact peak preservation (gap > p ≥ δ), I_-/I_+ safety, the stationary-call mass > 3/4 certificate with the caps argument, and gap persistence of the Min certificate through the upward pass.
- Lemma 5.3: q=D/128 < r/32 = D/64, and (8/5)·1 − (4/5)·(3/4) = 1 strict.
- The final induction, including the override precedence on I_- ∩ I_+.
- Sec. 6: the node count binom(ℓ,j)s^j with s=2048n+3, B0 = O(log n), and bit sizes of masses and pivots.
- Sec. 7: the bisection precision 2W·2^-K < 1/n², the value-preserving self-reduction for both players, and the amplification bound 2^{-r/2}.

Computational check: I implemented Label exactly as specified (memoized), ran it with D0 ∈ {8192, 32768} on 31 random games with n=2 and n=3 (which exercises the recursive case), and compared the winning sets against brute force over positional strategies. There were 0 mismatches.
main_claim: A deterministic algorithm computes the zero-threshold winning set of any mean-payoff game with binary-encoded integer weights in 2^{O(log² L)} bit operations. The method is a recursive simultaneous-labelling procedure on integer boxes using witness translation, stationary-pivot mass certificates and mass reweighting. Exact values and globally optimal positional strategies follow (Cor 7.1).
sibling_notes: The sibling 'Mean-payoff-parity-games-in-quasipolynomial-time-October-5-2026' was audited conditionally on this paper's Thm 1.1 and Cor 7.1 (liminf payoff, global positional strategies). I found both sound, so that condition is discharged. Cor 7.1 gives uniform positional strategies against history-dependent opponents, via the EM/Brim et al. uniform determinacy and the edge-subdivision transfer.
